2010-02-21: Brazil's ruling Workers' party nominated Dilma Rousseff, President Lula da Silva's chief of staff, to be its candidate in October's presidential election, raising the prospect of the country's first woman president.
2010-03-14: Dilma Rousseff clinched the ruling party's nomination for October's Brazilian presidential election and is riding high in the polls.
2010-10-03: Dilma Rousseff failed to win an outright majority in Brazil's presidential election, advancing to a runoff against José Serra.
Dilma Rousseff is poised to become Brazil's first female president as the country goes to the polls, with polls showing her leading with about 50%.
2010-10-31: Dilma Rousseff wins Brazil's presidential election, becoming the country's first female president with 56% of the vote.
2011-03-08: Dilma Rousseff is described as Brazil's first female president, having been inaugurated after promising economic stability and poverty reduction.
2011-11-02: Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff is expected to bring harsh criticism of Europe's handling of the debt crisis to the G20 meeting in Cannes.
2011-12-02: Nearly a year after being elected Brazil's first female president, Dilma Rousseff's pledge to empower women appears to be materializing, with a record number of female candidates preparing to stand in 2012 mayoral elections in her home state of Minas Gerais.
2013-09-18: Dilma Rousseff postponed an official visit to Washington to meet with Barack Obama due to the lack of a timely investigation into reports that the US National Security Agency spied on her phone calls and emails and those of Petrobras.
2014-10-02: Dilma Rousseff is poised to win both the first and second rounds of Brazil's presidential election, according to an article analyzing her likely victory.
2014-10-05: Dilma Rousseff topped the first round of Brazil's presidential election with 41.59% of the vote and will face Aécio Neves in a runoff on 26 October.
2014-10-12: Marina Silva endorses Aécio Neves for president, dealing a blow to Dilma Rousseff's re-election hopes ahead of the 26 October runoff.
2014-10-26: Incumbent Dilma Rousseff is set to face Aécio Neves in a runoff vote in Brazil's presidential election, with polls showing her as the favourite.
Dilma Rousseff is re-elected president of Brazil after securing more than 51% of votes against rival Aécio Neves.
2014-12-24: Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff appointed controversial agribusiness advocate Kátia Abreu as agriculture minister, drawing criticism from environmentalists.
2015-02-04: Petrobras chief executive Maria das Graças Foster, hand-picked by President Dilma Rousseff, resigned along with five senior directors amid a widening corruption scandal, adding pressure on Rousseff.
2015-03-15: Hundreds of thousands of protesters across more than 60 Brazilian cities called for the impeachment of President Dilma Rousseff amid corruption and economic grievances.
2015-03-16: The treasurer of Brazil's ruling Workers' Party was formally charged with corruption, adding pressure on President Dilma Rousseff.
2015-07-16: Lower house speaker Eduardo Cunha warns that Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff could face impeachment proceedings, saying he will decide within 30 days whether to move forward.
2015-08-13: Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff faces mass anti-government protests calling for her impeachment amid a corruption scandal, economic troubles, and record-low approval ratings.
2015-08-16: Hundreds of thousands of Brazilians take to the streets demanding the impeachment of President Dilma Rousseff.
2015-08-23: People in Brazil protested against President Dilma Rousseff.
2015-10-02: Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff cut her own salary by 10%, slashed eight ministries, and reshuffled her cabinet in an attempt to ward off an escalating political and economic crisis.
2015-12-02: Lower house speaker Eduardo Cunha launched impeachment proceedings against Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff over allegations she broke fiscal laws by window dressing government accounts ahead of her re-election.
2015-12-03: Allies of Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff rally congressional supporters to head off a possible impeachment vote after the lower house speaker approved a case against her.
2015-12-08: Vice President Michel Temer sent a letter to President Dilma Rousseff complaining of being given only a decorative role, and later said he believed there were legal grounds for the impeachment motion against her.
Brazil's supreme court suspended the creation of an impeachment committee against President Dilma Rousseff until a ruling on the legality of the secret ballot that appointed it.
2016-03-13: More than a million Brazilians joined anti-government rallies across the country, increasing pressure on embattled President Dilma Rousseff amid an impeachment challenge, a severe recession, and a major corruption scandal.
2016-03-16: Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff appointed former president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva as her chief of staff amid an attempted cabinet reshuffle to stay in office.
2016-03-17: Brazil's congress elected the 65 members of a special commission that will examine the case to impeach Dilma Rousseff, who is accused of using illegal accounting manoeuvres to balance the government's books.
2016-03-18: Federal deputies began debating Dilma Rousseff's impeachment fate in extraordinary sessions aimed at forcing a vote by mid-April, as she faced an impeachment threat in Congress.
2016-03-23: Dilma Rousseff gave a 90-minute interview with six foreign media organizations at the presidential palace, insisting there is no legal justification for her impeachment and warning that removing her from power illegally would leave lasting scars on Brazilian democracy.
2016-03-31: More than 100,000 demonstrators joined protests in dozens of Brazilian cities against what they see as a coup against President Dilma Rousseff.
2016-04-07: A former construction executive testified in a plea bargain that the Belo Monte dam was used to generate 150m reais in donations to Brazil's ruling coalition, adding pressure on President Dilma Rousseff.
2016-04-11: Sections of Brazil's rightwing opposition are attempting to impeach and oust President Dilma Rousseff, efforts the letter's signatories describe as undemocratic.

A Brazilian congressional committee voted 38 to 27 to proceed with an impeachment motion against President Dilma Rousseff over allegations of manipulating government accounts before the 2014 election, setting the stage for a full lower house vote.
2016-04-16: Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff fought a last-ditch battle against impeachment on the eve of a lower house vote, while her deputy Michel Temer campaigned to replace her.
2016-04-17: Brazil's lower house of Congress voted to impeach President Dilma Rousseff, advancing the case to the Senate.
2016-04-18: Brazil's lower house voted to send the impeachment motion against President Dilma Rousseff to the senate.
2016-04-19: Dilma Rousseff said it was "lamentable" that one of her accusers, Jair Bolsonaro, had glorified the torture used against her and others during Brazil's dictatorship era.
2016-04-20: Impeachment proceedings against Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff are underway, with the article discussing the potential global fallout and damage to Brazil's international standing.
2016-04-22: Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff told journalists in New York there is no legal foundation for her impeachment, calling it a coup and vowing to fight to remain in office.
2016-04-28: Dilma Rousseff acknowledged she may not play any official role during the Olympic Games if the senate passes an impeachment motion against her.
2016-05-03: Brazil's prosecutor general reportedly accused President Dilma Rousseff of obstructing justice, an allegation she denies, which could lead to a criminal investigation if accepted by the supreme court.
2016-05-05: The Brazilian Senate voted to impeach President Dilma Rousseff, suspending her for 180 days while senators decide whether to permanently remove her from office.
2016-05-09: Dilma Rousseff is expected to be ejected from the Planalto palace this week.
Brazil's newly appointed lower house speaker Waldir Maranhão proclaimed the annulment of last month's impeachment vote against Dilma Rousseff, a move immediately challenged by senior senate figures.
2016-05-11: Brazil's Senate votes to launch an impeachment trial against suspended President Dilma Rousseff, who condemns the move as a "coup."
2016-05-12: The Senate voted 55-22 to suspend Dilma Rousseff from the presidency and begin an impeachment trial.
2016-05-13: Dilma Rousseff is on trial in an impeachment process that is seen by many as a controversial "soft coup."
2016-05-26: The suspension of President Dilma Rousseff in Brazil is condemned as an insult to democracy by MPs and civil society groups.
2016-07-05: Feminists in Brazil continue to protest against the sexist impeachment of Dilma Rousseff and express solidarity with her.
2016-08-29: Brazil's suspended president Dilma Rousseff testified in her own defense before the Senate in her impeachment trial, denouncing the process as a coup and proclaiming her innocence.
2016-08-30: Dilma Rousseff was removed from Brazil's presidency by the Senate after impeachment, though the Senate did not strip her of her political rights.
2016-08-31: Brazil's Senate voted 61 to 20 to convict and remove President Dilma Rousseff from office, ending 13 years of Workers' Party rule; the Senate separately voted 42 to 36 not to bar her from public office for eight years.
2016-10-19: Eduardo Cunha, the Brazilian politician who orchestrated the impeachment of former president Dilma Rousseff, was arrested on corruption charges.
2016-11-10: Lawyers for former Brazilian president Dilma Rousseff presented evidence to the supreme electoral court suggesting her successor, Michel Temer, accepted bribes from construction company Andrade Gutierrez.
